+# Defend Against Threats - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn
+
+Prepare your security operations for AI by connecting threat detection, investigation, and response in Microsoft Defender.
+
+## Security imperative: Get ready for AI
+
+Defending against threats to get ready for AI starts with your existing security operations: bring signals, investigations, and response together, expand visibility across Microsoft and non-Microsoft sources, and automate repeatable work.
+
+### Job to be done: Defend against threats
+
+That foundation is what lets human defenders and AI agents investigate and respond together, while helping the organization keep pace with AI-accelerated attacks. Defender ISOC supports this by unifying SIEM and XDR in one operational experience built on shared data, analytics, threat intelligence, and workflows.
+
+## Context and problem
+
+AI is shrinking the window from intrusion to impact—and expanding the number of targets attackers can pursue at once.
+
+AI is helps attackers find and connect weaknesses organizations already carry: over-permissioned identities, unpatched software, exposed assets, and inadequately protected data. Addressing vulnerabilities in isolation—such as prioritizing software patches alone—no longer delivers the same impact. Nor can a collection of robust controls stop attackers who move across domains. Getting ready for AI requires a connected system that can uncover, understand, and adapt to threats before attackers turn a chain of exposures into a viable attack path.
+
+## Solution
+
+Getting ready for AI requires strengthening how you defend the environment you already have. Unify security signals and workflows, connect the data sources most relevant to your estate, and give defenders one place to investigate incidents, understand activity, automate response, and verify that threats have been contained. This foundation enables AI agents and human defenders to investigate and respond together effectively.
+
+Five sequential steps can get you there: deploy comprehensive protection, set up automatic attack disruption, respond to and contain incidents, prevent recurrence, and continuously optimize protection to reduce exposure. Comprehensive coverage improves detection, automated disruption limits attacker movement, and lessons from each incident help strengthen protection against the next attack.
+
+## Guidance
+
+Security practitioners, including SOC analysts, threat hunters, detection engineers, and incident responders, can strengthen threat defense by following this step-by-step guidance, implemented through Microsoft Defender.
+
+### Step
+
+1. Deploy Defender workloads for comprehensive protection
+
+#### Recommended action
+
+    Deploy the Defender workloads relevant to your environment across endpoints, identities, email and collaboration, and cloud apps so Microsoft Defender can correlate threat signals and coordinate prevention, detection, investigation, and response across those domains.
+
+#### Resource
+
+    [Setup guides for Microsoft Defender](deploy-configure-m365-defender)
+2. Set up attack disruption to detect and contain active attacks
+
+#### Recommended action
+
+    Review the licensing, permissions, and product-specific prerequisites for automatic attack disruption, then deploy and configure the required Defender workloads so compromised assets can be automatically contained during high-confidence attacks.
+
+#### Resource
+
+    [Configure automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender](configure-attack-disruption)
+3. Respond to incidents and validate the threat containment
+
+#### Recommended action
+
+    Triage and investigate incidents in the Defender portal, contain and eradicate the threat, recover affected resources to a trusted state, and validate that the threat is no longer active before resolving the incident.
+
+#### Resource
+
+    [Plan an incident response workflow in the Microsoft Defender portal](plan-incident-response)
+4. Hunt for related and recurring activity.
+
+#### Recommended action
+
+    Hunt across Defender data for related or recurring activity, then turn what you learn into custom detections that continuously identify and respond to suspected breach activity and other findings.
+
+#### Resource
+
+    [Advanced hunting overview in Microsoft Defender](advanced-hunting-overview)
+5. Optimize protection to reduce exposure
+
+#### Recommended action
+
+    Use SOC optimization recommendations to identify gaps in security coverage and adjust controls and data as threats and business priorities change, helping continuously reduce exposure across the environment.
+
+#### Resource
+
+    [Optimize security operations](/en-us/azure/sentinel/soc-optimization/soc-optimization-access?tabs=defender-portal)
+
+## Outcomes
+
+- **Help reduce the risk that exposures become attacks:** connected context reveals how vulnerabilities, identities, permissions, assets, and data create attack paths, helping teams close the gaps that pose the greatest risk before attackers exploit them.
+- **Help contain attacks and limit their spread:** shared signals across identity, devices, data, applications, cloud, and code enable coordinated detection and response instead of isolated action from point tools.
+- **Use incident learnings to strengthen future defenses:** teams verify that remediation took effect, measure the exposure that remains, and feed lessons from investigations back into protections, priorities, and response workflows.
+
+## Key success factors
+
+To measure progress, consider tracking the following metrics:
+
+- Percentage of identities, devices, applications, workloads, data, and AI systems covered by security policy and protection, with unmanaged or unprotected assets identified
+- Percentage of critical assets and sensitive data mapped to their related vulnerabilities, identities, permissions, and attack paths
+- Percentage of high-priority exposures assigned to an accountable owner and approved remediation or compensating-control action
+- Percentage of high-priority attack paths broken through patching, access reduction, configuration changes, data protection, or other controls
+- Percentage of prioritized remediation actions verified as effective, with remaining exposure measured
+- Mean time to detect, investigate, contain, and evict active threats across the environment
+- Percentage of incidents whose findings result in updated exposure priorities, detections, controls, or automated response workflows
+
+## Summary
+
+Defending against threats to get ready for AI changes the question from how many alerts you can process to how quickly you can detect, contain, and learn from attacks. Deploy Defender workloads across your environment, prepare automatic attack disruption to contain active threats, respond to and fully remediate incidents, hunt for related activity to prevent recurrence, and continually optimize protection to reduce exposure. Together, these steps create a continuous defense cycle that gets stronger as threats and the environment change.
+
+**By connecting threat response with continuous exposure reduction, you strengthen the environment for AI and make each defense improve the next.**

+## Intermittent failures in the SAP logging pipeline
+
+Brief network interruptions, SAP system downtime, or temporary resource constraints can cause a collection request to fail. The agentless data connector automatically retries failed collection windows, so a failed request doesn't immediately mean that logs are permanently lost.
+
+### Automatic retries and checkpoints
+
+The Microsoft Sentinel poller uses the Codeless Connector Framework (CCF) to request logs for collection windows bounded by `startTimeUTC` and `endTimeUTC`. When a window fails:
+
+- The poller retries the same `startTimeUTC` and `endTimeUTC` window according to the configured request retry count. If those retries fail, the poller waits before attempting the same window again. This delay is called backoff.
+- Checkpoint advancement occurs only after successful ingestion. A failed window isn't marked as successfully ingested.
+- Later collection windows continue without waiting for the failed window to succeed. The failed window remains eligible for retries, even when newer logs are arriving.
+
+For example, if collection fails for the five-minute window from 10:00 to 10:05 UTC and the configured retry count is three, the poller retries that window three times. If all three retries fail, the poller waits before attempting the same window again. Meanwhile, later collection windows can continue. When a retry succeeds, logs from 10:00 to 10:05 UTC are ingested later. The next scheduled collection doesn't replace the retry for the failed interval.
+
+For background on CCF query windows and request-level retry settings, see the [RestApiPoller data connector reference](../data-connector-connection-rules-reference). Request-level retry settings aren't the same as the failed-window recovery limit described next.
+
+### Seven-day automatic recovery limit
+
+The poller retries a failed collection window for up to seven days. If the window can't complete successfully within that period, automatic retries no longer recover it, and a permanent ingestion gap can remain unless you recover the missing logs manually.
+
+### Investigate and recover a failed window
+
+To check recovery and address persistent failures:

messageCenterItems.title: Retirement notice: MDE and XDR Advanced Hunting APIs retiring; migrate to Microsoft Graph Security API
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft is retiring the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Defender XDR Advanced Hunting APIs by February 1, 2027. Organizations must manually migrate workflows to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31, 2027, to ensure continued functionality and improved security integration.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated this post as a reminder. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

We’re retiring the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) Advanced Hunting API and Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting API and transitioning customers to the Microsoft Graph Security API. This update aligns our security integrations with a unified interface and schema across Microsoft Defender products. The Microsoft Graph Security API provides broader data coverage, improved consistency, and better scalability for automation and security workflows.

When this will happen 

  • Retirement start: February 6, 2026 
  • Full retirement: February 1, 2027 
  • After February 1, 2027, the MDE and XDR APIs will no longer function.

How this affects your organization

Who is affected: 

  • Organizations using the MDE or XDR Advanced Hunting API for automation, integration, or custom workflows.
  • You are receiving this message because our reporting indicates your organization may be using these APIs.

What will happen:

  • The MDE and XDR Advanced Hunting APIs will stop functioning after February 1, 2027.
  • Existing scripts, automations, and workflows that rely on these APIs will fail if not updated.
  • The Microsoft Graph Security API will be the supported API for accessing Microsoft security data.
  • No automatic migration will occur; manual updates will be required.

What you can do to prepare

  • Migrate all existing API workflows to the Microsoft Graph Security API by January 31, 2027.
  • Update internal documentation, automation scripts, and integration endpoints to use the Microsoft Graph Security API.
  • Communicate these changes to your security operations, engineering, and development teams.
  • Review Microsoft documentation to plan your migration: Use the Microsoft Graph security API.
  • If your organization uses custom solutions, validate that new queries and response schemas work as expected before the retirement date.

Learn more:

  • Advanced hunting - Use the Microsoft Graph security API | Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn
  • Migrate from the older APIs - Use the Microsoft Graph security API | Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn
  • (to be retired) Advanced Hunting API - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint | Microsoft Learn
  • (to be retired) Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting API - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: New MessageContents table in Advanced Hunting for Microsoft Teams messages
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 introduces a new MessageContents table in Advanced Hunting for Teams messages, enabling authorized security analysts to query message snippets and metadata for threat investigations. Rollout is from late September to mid-November 2026. Access requires specific permissions and may impact security procedures.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

We're introducing a new MessageContents table in Advanced Hunting for Microsoft Teams messages. This new table helps security operations teams investigate threats in Teams by providing access to Teams message snippets and associated message metadata during threat investigations.

This capability enhances security investigations by allowing authorized analysts to correlate Teams message activity with other security signals available in Advanced Hunting, helping organizations detect, investigate, and respond to threats more effectively.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late September 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously mid-October)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Security administrators and security analysts who use Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting
  • Organizations that investigate security incidents involving Microsoft Teams communications

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Defender XDR
  • Microsoft Defender for Office 365
  • Microsoft Teams
  • Advanced Hunting

What will happen

  • A new MessageContents table will become available in Advanced Hunting.
  • Authorized users will be able to query Teams message snippets and related message metadata.
  • Analysts can correlate Teams message information with other Advanced Hunting data sources during investigations.
  • The table can contain Teams message content, so access is permission controlled.
  • Users must have the required Advanced Hunting and message preview permissions to access and query the table. Users without the required permissions will not have access to the table.
  • Users without the required permissions will not have access to the table.
  • The table currently supports Teams messages available through the underlying Teams message metadata source, including messages containing URLs and federated messages.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required if your organization does not plan to use this capability.

If you plan to use this feature:

  • Review existing role assignments and determine which security administrators and analysts should have access to Teams message content for security investigations.
  • Review the required Advanced Hunting and message preview permissions before providing access.
  • Consider updating internal security investigation procedures and documentation.

Learn more

  • Advanced hunting overview in Microsoft Defender XDR - Microsoft Defender XDR | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations
